summary: the reduced mass, the angular frequency and the period of two masses joined by a harmonic bond, in an engine's own self-consistent units

inputs.name: force_constant
inputs.meaning: k of the bond's energy U = k (r - r0)^2 / 2, the potential constant an MD engine's harmonic bond takes

inputs.name: mass_a
inputs.meaning: the mass of one of the two bonded particles

outputs.name: reduced_mass
outputs.meaning: mass_a mass_b / (mass_a + mass_b), the single mass whose motion is the pair's relative motion

outputs.name: angular_frequency
outputs.meaning: the square root of the force constant over the reduced mass

outputs.name: period
outputs.meaning: 2 pi over the angular frequency: the time of one oscillation of the bond's length

validity: a harmonic bond between two point masses in classical mechanics, with no other force on them; an anharmonic bond's period depends on the amplitude, and a bond whose vibrational quantum is large beside kT is not classical, which this skill does not judge

source.citation: HyperPhysics (R. Nave, Georgia State University), Simple Harmonic Motion (read 2026-11-21, http://hyperphysics.phy-astr.gsu.edu/hbase/shm2.html; mat-20261121-hyperphysics-shm); HyperPhysics (R. Nave, Georgia State University), Reduced Mass (read 2026-11-21, http://hyperphysics.phy-astr.gsu.edu/hbase/orbv.html, section Reduced Mass; mat-20261121-hyperphysics-reduced-mass)
source.locus: Simple Harmonic Motion: angular frequency = sqrt(spring constant / mass), and with the period T the angular frequency is 2 pi / T; Reduced Mass: the relative motion of two masses under a central force is that of a single mass mu = m1 m2 / (m1 + m2) (the section's equation image)

note: Written for the HOOMD-blue agent of meta_agent/tasks/031, whose time step is to resolve the bond it received: the period is given in the engine's own units, from a force constant and masses in them, so that no scale of the engine's time is needed. No value of either source stands behind the worked cases; each is worked by hand in its worked field, on two unrelated kinds of system.
